source: FAO / Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) / Australian Government AusAID, coconut beetle biological-control trifold leaflet, published 2005
text: The leaflet notes that a healthy coconut palm supports household use and small handicraft production from its various parts, illustrated with photos of woven baskets, a woven mat/decorative panel, wooden spoons and forks, and carved coconut-shell bowls and figures. These household products (ផលិតផលប្រើប្រាស់កសិកម្មពីដើមដូង) made from coconut leaves, husk fiber, wood, and shell represent one of the reasons cited for protecting coconut palms from beetle damage — a healthy, undamaged palm sustains both fruit yield and this by-product/handicraft value for farming households.
